  • Assertion: The slowest elementary step in a complex reaction decides the rate of the reaction.
     
  • Reason: The slowest elementary step always has the smallest molecularity.

     
C. Concept
  • In a complex reaction, the rate-determining step (RDS) is the slowest step, and it controls the overall rate of the reaction.
     
  • Molecularity refers to the number of molecules involved in an elementary step (unimolecular, bimolecular, etc.).
     
  • Molecularity does not necessarily determine the speed of a reaction step. A step with lower molecularity isn’t always slower, and vice versa.

  • The Assertion is true: The rate of a complex reaction is controlled by its slowest step (rate-determining step).
     
  • The Reason is false: The slowest step does not always have the smallest molecularity. Many factors like activation energy affect the rate.

     
E. Final Answer
Option 3: Assertion is true statement but Reason is false"
